<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Add an opt-in `KVCacheSpec.get_kv_cache_transfer_regions(actual_cache)` contract returning named storage-sharing views in fixed logical `[B,H,N,C]` order. Backend-specific storage adaptation belongs to the producer; connector registration signatures remain unchanged.

Contract: [vllm-project/vllm #64388](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64388) (`717cb2da70f03c7d8f35b61225d08da9c1f40585`). Producer: [RBLN-SW/vllm-rbln #1361](https://github.com/RBLN-SW/vllm-rbln/pull/1361) (`0cbc0453d74b082649c0fb004eb642d7da0f7399`). Consumer: [LMCache/LMCache #6155](https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/pull/6155) (`c0f763e0306164db1e536f36860c24d68bf30628`).

## Claims

- Default specs return `None` and retain existing registration behavior. Dense producers can expose separate `key` and `value` region views with real strides and storage offsets.
- This is a new three-file proposal, independent of [the axis-descriptor proposal #63699](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63699), which remains unchanged and under discussion. No runner or MultiConnector propagation is added here.
- The companion RBLN exporter projects either `[B,2,H,1,N,D]` or `[2,B,H,1,N,D]` without repacking, even at `B=2`. LMCache's companion production connector consumes those views and restores original storage.

## Validation

Exact head `717cb2da70f03c7d8f35b61225d08da9c1f40585`, based on main `36d4ef654a83e227216b0c0b55cf4041d96b1675`. In a [vLLM CPU development environment](https://github.com/maobaolong/vllm/blob/717cb2da70f03c7d8f35b61225d08da9c1f40585/docs/contributing/README.md) with pytest/tblib installed:

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu PYTHONPATH="$PWD" python -m pytest --noconftest \
  tests/v1/test_kv_cache_spec_registry.py -q
# 48 passed; 1 source-tree missing-version warning
pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/kv_cache_interface.py \
  tests/v1/test_kv_cache_spec_registry.py docs/design/attention_backends.md
```

Applicable hooks passed. The full/MLA default-contract cases fail when the method is removed. The existing CPU registry CI step selects this test file. No default inference allocation or execution path calls the method, and no model-output change is claimed. `--noconftest` isolates source-level checks, not serving validation.

A separate CPU harness passed 16 cases using actual RBLN spec classes, actual vLLM `KVCacheConfig`, and real LMCache `EngineDrivenTransferContext.register/submit_store/submit_retrieve`, production gather/scatter and tensor wire. Only the network client is mocked. Another 2-case check constructs the real `LMCacheMPConnector` with real `VllmConfig`, resolves layout through the public vLLM resolver, and calls its registration entrypoint; only the external worker adapter is mocked. These source checks bypass RBLN SDK package initialization and do not establish full server/NPU E2E or performance.

[Download the English/中文 illustrated review guide](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34108425/spec-transfer-regions-suite-review.html) — one offline HTML, language switch, diagrams, code/test walkthrough, source harnesses, and comparison with the original axis proposal.

## Details

This is an alternative to arbitrary axis semantics at registration, not a revision replacing #63699. It follows #42082's fixed logical consumer ordering, but still adds a public method to `KVCacheSpec`; upstream acceptance and placement are open questions.

This API constructs regions from actual native storage. The unmerged #46387 (`a1c222e4773565f19c938211d6817a402c61adf5`) handles TP slicing of already-known BHNC regions. This proposal does not duplicate its slicing implementation or claim that integration with its final API is settled.

The vLLM base method formalizes the shared contract; it is not a strict runtime dependency of this Python implementation. RBLN defines the exporter on its subclass and LMCache discovers it optionally, so the producer/consumer pair can execute before the base method lands. Upstream agreement on the API and supported-version validation remain review/merge gates.

Dense unquantized K/V, both MP transfer modes on capable platforms, whole-block local-partition transfers. CPU/CUDA support native-owner handle registration; RBLN retains engine-driven mode because its current platform lacks IPC/event support. Kernel-block subdivision is explicitly rejected: native states per block must equal the spec block size. No arbitrary Mamba/quantized codec, heterogeneous TP conversion, unaligned token range, or in-process connector support is added. Region creation aliases storage; transfer and serialization can copy. The new RBLN consumer branch uses shared torch tensor ops and has not been performance-tested on NPU. The original native-format route may retain a lower-risk path to existing optimized operations; performance superiority is not claimed here.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex assisted with implementation, source validation, and review. All three companion PRs remain Draft for human review and API discussion. Original #63699, RBLN #1297, LMCache #6072 and PoC #6145 are unchanged.

@@ -241,3 +241,27 @@ default on NVIDIA is `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV4` on SM12x and
 `FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV4` on other supported CUDA architectures.
 
 --8<-- "gen:table-mla-v4-decode"
+
+## Exporting transfer regions from custom storage
+
+A backend can override `KVCacheSpec.get_kv_cache_transfer_regions(kv_cache)` to
+expose named views of its actual per-layer cache. Each region has logical order
+`[blocks, heads, states, content]`; physical strides and storage offsets may
+differ. Region construction must share the registered cache's storage, so
+writes through a returned view update the cache used by attention.
+
+Dense attention exports `{"key": key_view, "value": value_view}`. Content remains
+spec-owned: names do not define a quantization codec or permit consumers to
+reinterpret compressed state as dense K/V. Specs without an override return
+`None`, preserving existing registration behavior.
+
+For `[B, 2, H, 1, N, D]` storage, a producer can export
+`cache[:, 0, :, 0]` and `cache[:, 1, :, 0]`; for `[2, B, H, 1, N, D]`, it can
+export `cache[0, :, :, 0]` and `cache[1, :, :, 0]`. Both produce `[B, H, N, D]`
+regions without copying or merging K/V into one dimension. A connector obtains
+the spec from its existing `KVCacheConfig` and calls this method at registration,
+before normalization. `register_kv_caches` keeps its existing signature.
+
+This export maps native storage to standard regions. TP slicing of those regions
+is a separate operation; it does not replace `slice_for_tp_transfer` in the
+[multi-view connector work](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46387).

+    cache = torch.zeros((2, 1, 4, 16))
